rows.name: NSF fee rules (personal accounts at federally regulated banks)
rows.summary: For personal deposit accounts at federally regulated banks: NSF fees capped at $10; at most one NSF fee per account in a period of 2 business days; no NSF fee when the account would be overdrawn by less than $10. Provincially regulated credit unions set their own fees.

source.name: Financial Consumer Agency of Canada, news release

rows.inBerry: When a simulated debit is returned NSF, Berry shows the borrower's own bank fee: these rules for personal accounts at banks; for credit union accounts an illustrative fee, labelled 'provincially regulated — fee illustrative'. Retries are never scheduled inside the 2-business-day window. Business days are weekdays only (holidays not modelled).

rows.name: Payments Canada Rule H1: pre-authorized debits
rows.summary: Rules for pre-authorized debit (PAD) agreements: mandatory agreement elements (Appendix II), confirmation at least 10 calendar days before the first debit, 10 days' pre-notification of changes and variable amounts, prominent waiver clauses, cancellation, and recourse of 90 calendar days (personal) or 10 business days (business).
rows.inBerry: Repayment schedules follow the confirmation and pre-notification timing; the agreement checklist shows every Appendix II mandatory element and the verbatim recourse statement.
rows.note: Appendix IV (confirmation wording) was only skimmed; Berry does not reproduce it.

rows.name: Payments Canada Standard 005: AFT file format
rows.summary: Fixed-width file format for automated funds transfer, encoded in EBCDIC, with record types including header (A), credit (C), debit (D) and trailer (Z) records of 1,464 characters. The standard defines others that Berry doesn’t use.
rows.inBerry: Berry generates a sample disbursement file in the A, C and Z layouts from the standard, in ASCII rather than EBCDIC. Illustrative: not for submission.
rows.note: Amounts in cents and the mandatory flag on some credit-record fields are inferred from the standard's sample and tables, not stated outright.

rows.name: AFT and PAD return reason codes (Standard 007)
rows.summary: Three-digit codes on returned AFT and PAD items, e.g. 901 NSF (Debit Only), 903 Payment Stopped/Recalled, 905 Account Closed, 907 No Debit Allowed, 914 Incorrect Payor/Payee Name. The standard applies to both AFT and ISO AFT transactions.
rows.inBerry: Simulated returned debits use these codes with their official labels. Which returns Berry retries (only 901 and 908) and which come back before settlement is Berry's own illustrative policy.
rows.note: The standards don't say which return reasons may be re-presented, so Berry's retry policy by reason is illustrative.

rows.name: FINTRAC Large Cash Transaction Reports
rows.summary: Reporting entities report receiving $10,000 or more in cash in one transaction, or in two or more amounts within a consecutive 24-hour window by or for the same person or entity; reports are due within 15 calendar days.

source.name: FINTRAC, Large cash transaction reporting guidance

rows.inBerry: Cash deposits are checked for candidates and routed to a review queue. A compliance flag only, never a credit factor; Berry's report summary is illustrative, not a filing.

rows.name: CDIC deposit insurance
rows.summary: Eligible deposits at CDIC members are insured up to $100,000 per eligible category, per member institution. Members include banks and federally regulated credit unions; provincially regulated credit unions are not members.
rows.inBerry: Shown as context for deposit protection at Aspen Bank.

rows.name: Provincial credit union deposit insurance
rows.summary: Deposits at provincially regulated credit unions are protected by the deposit insurer of the credit union’s province, not CDIC. Coverage differs by province: confirmed limits range from $250,000 (per category, or per member in Prince Edward Island) to unlimited.
rows.inBerry: Northgate is described as a provincially regulated credit union whose coverage depends on its province; a per-province table shows only confirmed limits, with the rest marked Illustrative.
rows.note: BC, Ontario and Quebec limits could not be read from the official sites (access blocked) and are marked Illustrative in the table.

rows.name: Consumer-Driven Banking Act
rows.summary: The legal framework for consumer-driven (open) banking. Most provisions, including consent, are not yet in force; regulations are required to bring the Act into force.
rows.effective: Royal assent March 26, 2026 (S.C. 2026, c. 3, s. 224); most provisions not yet in force

source.name: Justice Laws Website, Consumer-Driven Banking Act

rows.inBerry: Berry's consent screen and dashboard are built around the framework's consent principles. Berry is not accredited and connects to no real institution.

rows.name: Consent duration: at most 12 months
rows.summary: Express consent may be valid for no more than 12 months after it is obtained (Act s. 86), with renewal within seven days (s. 87); draft regulations add triggers for earlier renewal (s. 44).
rows.effective: Act s. 86, not yet in force

source.name: Justice Laws Website, Consumer-Driven Banking Act s. 86

rows.inBerry: Berry's simulated consents expire within 12 months and the consent screen says so.

rows.name: Consumer-Driven Banking Regulations
rows.summary: Proposed regulations: accreditation first, then read-only data sharing starting with deposit and payment accounts, then lending accounts, then registered and non-registered accounts. Write access (payment initiation) is left for a later phase; the screen-scraping prohibition will not come into force until further consultation.
rows.effective: Published for comment June 27, 2026 (Canada Gazette, Part I); comments closed after 60 days

source.name: Canada Gazette, Part I, Vol. 160, No. 26

rows.inBerry: Data requests are limited to what a decision needs, and the screen shows what was not requested.

rows.name: Technical standard for data sharing
rows.summary: The Minister of Finance will designate a technical standards body by order; the draft regulations do not name one.

source.name: Canada Gazette, Part I, Vol. 160, No. 26

rows.inBerry: Berry's transaction format is FDX-inspired. Berry does not claim FDX is Canada's standard.

rows.name: Real-Time Rail
rows.summary: Payments Canada's new real-time payment system, launching in Q4 2026 with the first direct participants; two sequential phases will then migrate Interac e-Transfer volumes.
rows.inBerry: Funding by Real-Time Rail is simulated. Lenders cannot fund on it today.

moreSources.name: Payments Canada, Q3 2026 quarterly update (participants and phases)

rows.name: Real-Time Rail: after the launch
rows.summary: Press reports expect every participant to have access to the Real-Time Rail some time in 2027. Payments Canada has not published dates for the phases after the Q4 2026 launch.
rows.inBerry: Mentioned as a press report only; no Berry feature depends on it.
rows.note: Press-reported, not from Payments Canada. Earlier versions of this row cited a 2027 Interac e-Transfer migration and Q3 2027 full capacity; no source we could read confirms either, so they were removed.

rows.name: Equifax Canada Global Consumer Credit File
rows.summary: Lets newcomers bring credit history from abroad; launched in October 2024 with India.
rows.inBerry: The 'foreign credit report available' toggle shows how an imported report changes each decision.
rows.note: The launch is confirmed from Equifax Canada’s October 2024 release; that the program still runs today is not re-confirmed.

rows.name: Foreign credit file coverage beyond India
rows.summary: Additional countries were announced as planned.
rows.inBerry: Berry says 'for example, India' and does not list other countries.
rows.note: No official confirmation found of countries added after launch.

rows.name: Foreign credit history at Scotiabank (with Nova Credit)
rows.summary: Scotiabank's newcomer program can use credit history from a listed set of countries, subject to change.
rows.inBerry: Context for why Berry's credit-building path fills the gap foreign reports don't cover.

rows.name: TransUnion and Nova Credit in Canada
rows.summary: A 2018 partnership to bring foreign credit history to Canadian lenders.
rows.note: Not reconfirmed as active; source is a third-party copy of the announcement.
